title: Full Color Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: Comparing Full Color Painting and Precision Paint Experts for a stucco or block home? Learn which crack repair and coating details to confirm on every bid.
h1: Full Color Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Stucco and concrete block behave differently from wood siding. This guide covers the masonry coating questions North Central Florida owners should ask.

questions: Should stucco be painted with elastomeric paint?
How are stucco cracks repaired before painting?

sections.h2: Masonry homes need a masonry plan
body: Full Color Painting is one of the painting and property-service companies homeowners in North Central Florida may be comparing. If your house is stucco over block, or you are painting a masonry wall, garage, or commercial building, the right questions are a little different from those for wood siding. Stucco moves, breathes, and cracks, and the coating has to work with that movement instead of fighting it.
This guide does not say anything about how other contractors approach masonry. It gives you a checklist to use with every bidder and explains the system Precision Paint Experts specifies.

sections.h2: Hairline cracks and how coatings handle them
body: Most stucco develops hairline cracks over time as the building settles and the wall heats and cools every day. A standard rigid paint film can split along those lines, letting water behind the coating. That is why we use elastomeric coatings on stucco with hairline movement. Elastomeric products build a thicker, flexible film that can bridge small cracks and stretch as the wall moves.

Larger cracks and damaged areas need repair before any coating goes on, because no paint will hide a structural crack for long. Our guide on dealing with stucco cracks explains the difference, and our article on stucco cracks in Lake City homes shows how the problem looks in the field.
Ask each contractor to answer these in writing:
bullets: Which cracks will be repaired, and how are larger repairs priced?
What primer or sealer goes on bare or patched masonry?
Is the topcoat elastomeric, 100% acrylic, or something else, and why?
How many coats, and will sprayed areas be back-rolled?
Will moisture be checked before coating begins?

sections.h2: How we specify stucco and masonry work
body: During the walkthrough our crew lead photographs the walls, notes crack patterns, and takes moisture readings where water may be getting in. The estimate then lists the repair scope, the primer and topcoat products by name, and the coat count. Two full coats is the baseline, with a third on porous surfaces, and sprayed areas are back-rolled where penetration matters.

Our stucco repair and painting service covers walls and repairs, and our concrete and masonry painting page addresses block walls, foundations, and other masonry. Where water intrusion is the larger concern, see our waterproofing and protective coatings.

Two stucco bids can look alike on price and still specify very different coatings and repair scopes. Put them side by side and compare the crack repair notes, the product names, and the coat counts. Our free estimate usually arrives within one business day of the walkthrough, and nothing is added to the job later without your written approval.

If a bid does not mention cracks at all, ask why. Either the walls are in unusually good shape, or the repair work has not been priced yet. Getting that answer now is far easier than negotiating it mid-job.

faqs.q: Is elastomeric paint always the right choice for stucco?
faqs.a: We use elastomeric on stucco with hairline movement, where its flexible film helps bridge small cracks. The product chosen for your walls is named on the estimate.

faqs.q: Do you repair stucco before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Crack and damage repair is scoped during the walkthrough and listed on the written estimate.

faqs.q: Do you work on block foundations and masonry walls too?
faqs.a: Yes. Concrete and masonry painting is one of our services, alongside stucco repair and protective coatings.
